emails.from_display: Maya D'Souza - Blue Arc Retail Customer Operations
emails.subject: [RP1-A07] URGENT: customer escalation - JOB-0701 must move today
emails.body:
Rhea,

This is now an escalation, not a routine status check. We were told this export was moving on MV Coral Wind and our receiving team has booked labour around that date. Your last note says the box may roll four days, but it gives us no replacement vessel, no confirmed space, and no answer we can pass to our buyer.

We need a concrete recovery plan before 15:00 Singapore time today. If the carrier cannot protect the next sailing, say that plainly and tell us what alternative you are actually securing. Please stop sending "checking" updates with no owner or time. I am very frustrated that the same booking has reached this point without a firm answer, and I will copy procurement if we miss the cutoff again.

Please acknowledge this escalation and come back with the carrier owner, the next decision time, and the customer-facing wording. Do not close this as resolved on a provisional ETA.
